transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-12 14:00 PST | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia (Redwood) - Rajesh, Emily, Darren, Olivia, Ben (Acme)

Summary: weekly POC check-in for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot. Focus: networking peering issues observed in staging, routing to dedicated nodes, runtime upgrade plan (2.1.3), and tuning KV cache / batching to hit P95 latency SLOs. Agreement on several follow-ups (network artifacts, staging dry-run of upgrade, benchmark schedule).

Topics: networking (VPC peering, TGW, NAT, NACLs), routing/failover, runtime upgrade, tuning parameters (batch size, prefix caching), security docs, next steps for pilot success.

Transcript: 
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll do the usual check-in, quick status and blockers - we have 48 minutes, does that still work?
00:08 Rajesh (Acme Infra): yes that works, I have to hop at the end around 14:45 but should be fine.
00:12 Liam (Redwood SE): quick agenda - network & routing findings from staging, runtime upgrade plan for 2.1.3, tuning notes on kv-cache and batching, then actions.
00:22 Olivia (Product): perfect, we want to focus on the peering flakiness and the p95 numbers from last week.
00:27 Sofia (CSM): I also have the security docs status to share briefly.
00:31 Emily (ML Platform): and I'll present the embedding latency numbers we ran yesterday.
00:35 Maya: great, Liam over to you for the network recap.
00:40 Liam (SE): yeah so in staging we saw intermittent 502s when traffic egressed via the TGW to the customer transit; initial root cause looks like asymmetric routing when the ephemeral test clients hit different NAT gateways - we think the problem is session affinity is not preserved across TGW attachments because of the on-prem firewall asymmetry. I collected flow logs and there's a mixture of return paths.
01:03 Ben (SRE): we noticed the same on our side; the route table for the peered subnet had the static route to the TGW but sometimes the return path went through the NAT instance in another AZ.
01:17 Rajesh: yep and our NACLs are fairly strict, so occasional dropped packets look like they cause TLS handshakes to fail and then the inference connection resets which Redwood interprets as a 502.
01:32 Liam: thanks, that explains the spike. short-term mitigation: set explicit source/destination check policy to false on the NAT instances and add stickiness via consistent egress ENIs, plus we recommended a TGW route fix — we'll send the exact rule diff.
01:49 Rajesh: that makes sense, we can apply in dev but want to confirm in staging first.
01:55 Maya: action item - Liam to send tcpdump and suggested iptables/routing diff; Rajesh to test in dev and report back.
02:04 Emily: quick note on results - embedding qps was stable but p95 latency for 512-token sequences hit 930ms at peak which is above your 800ms target. baseline (hosted) sat around 420ms for the same model.
02:26 Liam: thanks Emily - we suspect the P95 delta is from missing kv-cache hits and suboptimal batching. On Private you're seeing low cache hit rates because request affinity is getting split across multiple instances due to the routing. Once we fix the routing affinity, kv-cache hit rate should improve. Also we recommend increasing the continuous-batch size from 8 to 16 for this workload, and enabling per-customer prefix caching ttl of 60s given your re-use patterns.
02:52 Olivia: any risk on memory or GPU utilization with batch 16?
02:56 Liam: we saw about +6–8% GPU memory usage in our lab for batch 16 on the A100 40GB equivalent; throughput improved ~18% and p95 improved ~120ms in our synthetic runs. If you're constrained we can do a canary with one node group.
03:15 Darren (Security): can you confirm the runtime upgrade 2.1.3 includes the new FIPS crypto hooks? We need KMS integration tested, and audit logs.
03:25 Sofia: yes we have the security docs - last night I uploaded the SOC 2 excerpts and the KMS integration checklist to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.example.com/s/ACME-security).
03:36 Maya: brief on upgrades - 2.1.3 is primarily driver compatibility (CUDA 12.1) and a fix for kv-cache eviction bug seen on long-lived sessions. We recommend a staged upgrade: test on staging cluster with canary 10% traffic, monitor p50/p95 and connection stability for 24 hours, then roll to remaining nodes.
04:00 Ben: what is rollback plan if canary shows degraded latencies?
04:04 Liam: automatic fallback to previous runtime is supported, we also keep model-compatible variants and a routing policy that can reroute to hosted fallback for critical traffic. Rollback takes ~6–10 minutes to redirect the traffic if we trigger it manually.
04:20 Rajesh: ok good to know. one more ask: do you support BGP peering with our on-prem router, or is it only static routes through TGW?
04:29 Liam: currently we support TGW attachments and static routing for the pilot. BGP with direct router peering is on our roadmap but not in the pilot build. If you need dynamic BGP we can discuss an engineering exception, but it adds complexity to troubleshooting.
04:45 Emily: can you repeat recommended kv-cache ttl and batch settings?
04:48 Liam: kv-cache ttl 60s for prefix caching, continuous-batch size 16, and enable cache prefetch on hot routes. For tokenization, set request chunking to 256 tokens to avoid long tail spikes.
05:05 Olivia: that should help. any change required on client SDK?
05:09 Maya: we pushed a small client flag to enable prefix caching and it's backwards compatible; we'll provide the patch in the repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/client/PR-138).
05:22 Darren: security checklist - do we have RBAC controls for who can trigger runtime rollouts?
05:28 Sofia: yes, in Private the customer admin can restrict rollout permissions; we use SAML SSO + RBAC roles that map to admin/operator levels. I uploaded the mapping doc.
05:38 Rajesh: good. back to networking - Ben will run the tcpdump and share, I'll run the dev patch to the TGW routing and report results.
05:47 Ben: yes I'll capture the flows and share the pcap with Liam.
05:51 Liam: perfect. next on tuning: Emily, can you walk us through the embedding run?
05:56 Emily: sure — yesterday we ran 10k embeddings at 512 token average; throughput was 120 reqs/s, p50 210ms, p95 930ms, GPU util 62% averaged, memory stable. We saw bursts where p95 jumped to 1.2s when warmup miss on kv-cache.
06:21 Maya: those numbers align with what we saw; the warmup misses are consistent with the routing-affinity issue. After we address affinity, we expect p95 to drop into target range.
06:31 Olivia: timeline check — we want staging stable by end of next week to present to ops team. realistic?
06:37 Rajesh: if routing fix and small canary for upgrade go in early next week I think yes. but the TGW diff needs signoff.
06:45 Maya: ok plan: 1) Liam sends network diff + tcpdump (ASAP), 2) Rajesh/Ben test in dev by Thu 2/14, 3) Redwood schedules staging dry-run for 2/17-2/18, 4) benchmark run 2/20, 5) if good, move to wider pilot.
07:02 Olivia: agreed. anything else from Redwood?
07:06 Liam: just to call out cost tradeoff — if you want guaranteed low p95 we discussed Dedicated reserved pools instead of shared Private nodes; that's an option if peering/affinity remains brittle. AE can share costs.
07:21 Maya: I will share the Dedicated pricing options by tomorrow.
07:24 Darren: last sec on compliance — do you log plaintext prompts anywhere?
07:29 Sofia: no, by default Private keeps prompts ephemeral unless you opt into retention. Logs are encrypted and KMS-managed; details in the security doc.
07:38 Rajesh: ok thanks.
07:40 Maya: recap of action items and next steps (see notes) — any objections?
07:44 Olivia: none.
07:46 Maya: great, we'll follow up in slack and I'll create Jira tasks for the action items. Thanks everyone.
07:55 Rajesh: thanks all.
08:00 End of call.
